units.text: EXT. GLACIER CREVASSE CAMP - DAWN
A tent the color of a tangerine, pegged to blue ice.
Wind has dropped.
The world is pearl and silent.
HILDA (50s, frost in her eyebrows) kneels at a camp stove, coaxing a flame.
SOLVEIG (50s, same gray parka, same cropped silver hair) unrolls a map across her knees.
JAMAL (20s, hauling a coil of rope) crunches up from the edge, face wind-reddened.
Weather's holding.
units.name: JAMAL

units.text: Good. Then we eat.
units.name: HILDA

units.text: She stirs a pot.
Steam wisps.
Solveig traces a finger across the map and does not look up.
Jamal, how far to the saddle?
units.name: SOLVEIG

units.text: Two hours if the bridge holds.
units.name: JAMAL

units.text: Hilda, did you check the bridge?
units.name: SOLVEIG

units.text: Solveig, I checked it yesterday. She was fine.
units.name: HILDA

units.text: She?
units.name: JAMAL

units.text: Hilda and Solveig exchange a look.
Hilda's smile fades.
Solveig folds the map once.
Jamal. Where is the third rope?
units.name: SOLVEIG

units.text: Jamal glances at the coil in his hand.
Then at the edge.
A beat.
I left it anchored. For her.
units.name: JAMAL

units.text: Solveig stands.
Hilda lowers the spoon.
She looks at the pot, at the steam, at the tent, then at Jamal, who has begun, very slowly, to back away toward the crevasse.
Jamal. There wasn't a third climber.
units.name: HILDA

units.text: He stops.
The wind returns, and with it, faintly, from deep inside the ice, a woman's voice calling his name.
